evidence:
Scope: static weight honesty, not empirical judge discrimination or overall task clearance. Opened both actual frozen XLSX files with openpyxl. In each, Quality Checks row 45 (check 44) requires real functionality above structure/style; Internal Quality Checks row 45 explicitly interprets functionality as 60 percent plus its own relative criterion weights. Read the staged profile and quality-checks.md:178-179; the frozen profile expressly prescribes 0.6/0.2/0.2. Independently hashed all 84 manifest task/rule files: zero mismatches. All task citations below are relative to .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-postrepair-audit/task/.

Parsed all five judge.toml files and read every criterion, all three scored prompts, both gate prompts, context and public behavior notes. tests/scoring.toml:6-8 sets functional=0.6, polish=0.2, visual=0.2; line 11 sets the functional floor to 0.05. This policy is byte-identical to the frozen template policy. Both one-criterion gates use all_pass and have no positive dimension share. The 64 Functional criteria have total weight 32.7; seven Polish criteria total 4.0; six Visual criteria total 6.0. All criterion weights are positive, each scored dimension uses weighted_mean, and none of the five [judge] tables carries a hidden weight. Polish plus Visual can contribute at most 0.4, below Functional's 0.6. tests/tools/score.py:46-48 reads policy weights, requires functional strictly above its floor and rounds the final weighted value; tests/test.sh:217 and 227 call this scorer after the gate and scored suites.

The largest Functional weights establish the requested difficult product outcomes: literal-loop deadlines weight 2.75 (tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:150-154), restart durability weight 2.00 (346-350), stale-server refusal weight 1.80 (360-364), and dirty-draft retention/recovery weight 2.00 (367-371). These correspond directly to environment/instructions/behaviour.md:9 and 29 and integration.md:7. Their maximum final contributions are respectively about 5.05, 3.67, 3.30 and 3.67 percentage points. The three editor presentation criteria, explicitly requested at environment/instructions/ui.md:5, have much smaller weights: monospace 0.10, line numbers 0.15, syntax colouring 0.25 (functional/judge.toml:311-329). Even conservatively treating all three as nonfunctional presentation, they total only 0.5/32.7 of Functional, or 0.9174 percentage points of final reward; remaining Functional outcomes still carry 59.0826 percentage points versus 40.9174 for that broad presentation bucket. Functional/prompt.md:9 and 100 preserve separate outcome evidence rather than assigning a whole protocol's score; Polish/prompt.md:31 reserves execution and durable data to Functional; Visual/prompt.md:13-22 confines visual credit to rendered presentation. No source-structure or preferred-library criterion receives Functional credit.

Read-only execution: ran the actual frozen score.py main function with in-memory input/output path adapters, preserving its policy read and arithmetic and writing no task files. With both gates at 1: (F,P,V)=(1,0,0) produced reward 0.6; (0,1,1) produced 0; (0.05,1,1) produced 0; (0.06,1,1) produced 0.436; (0.5/32.7,1,1) produced 0; (1,1,1) produced 1. A failed Render gate produced 0. The 0.436 just above the functional floor is an explicit consequence of the required shared profile, not task-specific weight drift. Attempted broken witness: a beautifully presented editor satisfying only the three editor display rows cannot earn reward even when optimistically granting both gates and perfect Polish/Visual; its F=0.01529 is below the floor. An actually dead Run/save shell additionally fails the stated authored-run and independent-context save/read gates. Attempted conforming alternative: a fully working playground using native components, a restrained palette, accessible menus and a mobile drawer/tab arrangement remains eligible for full credit under the actual Polish/Visual descriptions; no weighting rule requires a particular implementation or layout. No credible false-pass or false-fail caused by weight allocation was found. These are source/scorer observations only: no full configured judge, Oracle, target-builder or empirical weak-app reward was run or inferred, and the raw-evidence index explicitly says those remain unmeasured.
